title: Luxembourg City, Fortress and Valley

bestPeriod.note: The Bock casemates and the palace tours are seasonal; both are shut for much of the winter.

summary: A week in the only capital where every bus, tram and train is free, spent climbing between a fortress plateau and the valleys 70 metres below.
hook: Luxembourg is a city with two floors. The plateau holds the banks, the palace and the ramparts; the Alzette and Pétrusse valleys, seventy metres down, hold the old mills, the abbey and the quiet. Nothing costs anything to reach, because since 2020 the whole country's public transport has been free.

snapshot.Base(s): Luxembourg City, single base all week
snapshot.Best Period: April to June, September and October
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: 55–70 km on foot with roughly 2,000 m of cumulative stair climbing
snapshot.Getting There: Findel airport, bus 16 to the centre in 25 min, free; TGV from Paris in 2h15
snapshot.Who It Suits: Fortification readers, architecture watchers, anyone who wants a capital they can finish

itinerary.title: Ville Haute and the UNESCO ramparts
itinerary.morning: Start on Place Guillaume II — the Knuedler — where the market runs Wednesday and Saturday mornings, roughly 08:00 to 14:00. Then the Grand Ducal Palace, a Spanish Renaissance town hall of 1573 whose state rooms open to guided tours only from mid-July to early September; tickets go on sale through the Luxembourg City Tourist Office at the end of June and are gone in days.
itinerary.afternoon: Notre-Dame Cathedral, a Jesuit church of 1613–21 with a 1930s neo-Gothic extension, then the Chemin de la Corniche along the old rampart wall. Batty Weber called it the most beautiful balcony in Europe and, looking down onto Grund, it is hard to argue.
itinerary.evening: Dinner on Rue de la Boucherie or Place d'Armes; the Chocolate House opposite the palace fills any gap beforehand.
itinerary.dayStats: 7 km walking, 180 m of stairs · districts: Ville Haute · tickets approx €14 (palace tour in season).

itinerary.title: The Bock, the Rham plateau and Grund
itinerary.morning: The Bock Casemates, cut by the Spaniards in 1644 and vastly extended under Vauban from 1684, run 17 km through the rock. Entry is approx €8; they open roughly from February to early November and the first hour is the only quiet one. The Pétrusse Casemates are separate, guided-only, about €15, and must be booked through the tourist office.
itinerary.afternoon: Follow the Wenzel Circular Walk, a signposted 2.5 km loop that drops from the Bock to the Alzette, crosses under the Rham plateau's barracks and comes back up through Grund. It is the clearest single explanation of how the fortress worked.
itinerary.evening: Neimënster in Grund — the 1606 abbey, later a prison, now a cultural centre with a courtyard bar and a concert programme. Ride the free Grund lift back up to Ville Haute from Plateau du Saint-Esprit.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walking, 300 m of stairs and ramps · districts: Bock, Rham, Grund · tickets approx €8.

itinerary.title: Pfaffenthal, Clausen and the Kirchberg plateau
itinerary.morning: Take the Pfaffenthal panoramic lift (2016), a free 71 m glass shaft from the Pescatore park down into the valley, then walk Pfaffenthal's Vauban towers and the Trois Glands. The free funicular from Pfaffenthal–Kirchberg station lifts you to the plateau.
itinerary.afternoon: Kirchberg is the country's architectural showroom. Mudam, I. M. Pei's 2006 museum built on the ruined Fort Thüngen, is approx €8; the Musée Dräi Eechelen inside the 1732 fort below it is free. Add Christian de Portzamparc's Philharmonie (2005) and Dominique Perrault's gold-clad Court of Justice towers (2008).
itinerary.evening: Down to Clausen and the Rives de Clausen, the converted Mousel brewery, for dinner and a beer under the rock.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking, 250 m of stairs · districts: Pfaffenthal, Kirchberg, Clausen · tickets approx €8.

itinerary.title: Gare quarter, Bonnevoie and the Pétrusse
itinerary.morning: Cross the Pont Adolphe (Paul Séjourné, 1903), for a while the largest stone arch bridge in the world, with its 2017 cycle-and-foot deck slung underneath. Then down into the Pétrusse valley park, reopened after several years of works, and along the stream bed under the viaducts.
itinerary.afternoon: The Gare quarter is the city's most mixed: Avenue de la Liberté's 1920s bank architecture, then Rue de Strasbourg and Bonnevoie's Portuguese and Cape Verdean grocers. Lunch here costs half what it does on the plateau.
itinerary.evening: Back up to Villa Vauban (1873), the city art museum built on a fort remnant, open late on Fridays.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walking, 200 m of stairs · districts: Gare, Bonnevoie, Pétrusse · tickets approx €5.

itinerary.title: Belval and Esch-sur-Alzette
itinerary.morning: Train to Belval-Université, about 25 minutes and free. Two blast furnaces of the old ARBED steelworks stand preserved in the middle of a new university quarter; Furnace A can be climbed on a guided visit booked through the Fonds Belval.
itinerary.afternoon: Esch-sur-Alzette, one stop on, is the second city and the heart of the Minett iron basin, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 2020. Walk Rue de l'Alzette for the Art Nouveau and Art Deco facades.
itinerary.evening: Back to the capital in half an hour; eat in the Gare quarter, where the trains land you.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walking · districts: Belval, Esch centre · tickets approx €0 (transport free, furnace tour approx €10).

itinerary.title: Vianden and the Our valley
itinerary.morning: Train to Ettelbruck (35 min), then bus 570 to Vianden (25 min). All free. Vianden Castle, an eleventh-to-fourteenth-century Ottonian and Gothic seat rebuilt from ruin between 1977 and the 1990s, is approx €10 and opens at 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: The chairlift climbs to a ridge café with the classic castle view; walk back down through the woods in 40 minutes. The Victor Hugo house by the bridge, where he stayed in 1871, is small and good.
itinerary.evening: Return by the same route; eat late in Grund or Clausen where the kitchens run past 22:00.
itinerary.dayStats: 7 km walking, 220 m ascent · districts: Vianden · tickets approx €10.

itinerary.title: Limpertsberg, the Glacis and a last Corniche circuit
itinerary.morning: Limpertsberg's villa streets and the Glacis field, where the Glacismaart takes over the third Sunday of each month from March to November: food, plants and flea stalls together.
itinerary.afternoon: The Lëtzebuerg City Museum, in a set of medieval houses on Rue du Saint-Esprit, approx €5, with a glass lift running down through four floors of rock.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Corniche once more at dusk and take the Grund lift down for a last dinner by the Alzette.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking, 150 m of stairs · districts: Limpertsberg, Glacis, Ville Haute · tickets approx €5.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Le Place d'Armes
accommodationStrategy.description: Seven joined historic houses on the main square, inside the pedestrian core, so every plateau day starts at the door and the Corniche is four minutes away. Its courtyard restaurant keeps a later kitchen than most of the Ville Haute.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 8–12 weeks ahead; avoid EU summit weeks entirely.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Parc Beaux-Arts
accommodationStrategy.description: Eleven suites in three eighteenth-century houses between the palace and the Bock. Quiet, and it puts the casemates and the Wenzel Walk literally below your window, which saves a lift ride each morning.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Vauban or the Gare-quarter chains
accommodationStrategy.location: Place Guillaume II and Avenue de la Liberté
accommodationStrategy.description: For a lower rate, stay near the station: trams and trains at the door, cheaper dinners in Bonnevoie, and a ten-minute walk or one free tram stop up to the plateau.

logistics.emergency: 112 for ambulance and fire, 113 for police. Pharmacies post the night rota (garde) in the window.
logistics.money: Cards work everywhere. Shops close at 18:00 or 19:00, and on Sunday almost everything but restaurants and the Grund bars is shut.
logistics.transportRules: Since 29 February 2020 all public transport in Luxembourg — bus, tram, train, the funicular and the Pfaffenthal lift — is free in second class, for everyone, with no ticket and no validation. First class on trains still requires a ticket (approx €3 for a day supplement).

other.label: Where free stops
other.text: At the border. Trains to Trier, Arlon, Thionville or Metz are free only to the last Luxembourgish station; buy the cross-border leg from CFL machines. The Pétrusse Express road train and guided tours are not public transport and are chargeable.

other.label: The tram
other.text: Line T1 runs Luxexpo–Kirchberg–Pont Rouge–Gare Centrale–Cloche d'Or. It is the fastest way between Kirchberg and the station and it is free.

other.label: The Luxembourg Card
other.text: costs roughly €13 for one day, €28 for three, and covers 90-plus sites nationwide. Because transport is already free, it only pays if you visit two or more ticketed sites in a day — on this itinerary, days 2, 3 and 6.

other.label: Opening traps
other.text: Most museums close Mondays; the Bock closes for winter; the palace opens for about seven weeks in summer. On National Day, 23 June, everything shuts and the city fills the night before.

other.label: Stairs
other.text: This is a vertical city. Lifts at Pfaffenthal, Grund and the Plateau du Saint-Esprit are free and run roughly 05:45 to 01:00; use them rather than the staircases when you are tired.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 for ambulance and fire, 113 for police. Pharmacies post the night rota (garde) in the window.

proTips: Do the Wenzel Walk anticlockwise: descend the Bock side in the morning, climb back through Grund in afternoon shade. The reverse means climbing into full sun.
Palace tour tickets go live at the tourist office on Place Guillaume II in late June for the whole season. Book the day they release or plan without them.
The Pfaffenthal lift is open around the clock and free, and at night the valley below it is lit — it is the best five-minute view in the city and nobody is there after 22:00.
Go to Belval on a weekday: the university quarter is alive and the furnace tours run. At weekends it is a ghost town.
Eat lunch in Bonnevoie or the Gare quarter: the same plate is €12 rather than €26.
If your dates cover a third Sunday, build them around the Glacismaart — it is the one day the capital feels crowded in a good way.

packingNotes: Shoes with grip and ankle tolerance: the Wenzel Walk and the casemates involve wet stone stairs.
A phone light for the deeper Bock galleries, which are lit but dim.
A light waterproof; the Alzette valley holds mist long after the plateau clears.
Warm mid-layer even in June — the casemates hold about 10°C year-round.
Smart-casual for dinner; the Ville Haute and Clausen dining rooms dress up more than the city's size suggests.
A small daypack only. Large bags are refused at Mudam and the casemates.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The casemates are closed for the season.** From roughly November to February the Bock is shut. Substitute the Musée Dräi Eechelen and the Lëtzebuerg City Museum, both indoor and both open year-round.
**You visit on a Monday.** Mudam, Villa Vauban, the City Museum and the national museum all close. Make Monday your Vianden or Belval day instead.
**The palace tour is sold out.** Usually it is. The guard change on Place du Palais and the free Dräi Eechelen museum cover the same history for nothing.
**Rail works north.** CFL replaces the Ettelbruck trains with buses some weekends, adding 20–30 minutes each way. Check cfl.lu the night before and leave an hour earlier.
**Sunday shutdown.** Shops close. Plan Sunday around Grund, the Corniche, Neimënster and the Glacismaart, and buy food on Saturday.
